title: Voyager 1 Goes Silent Just as It Hits a Record Distance
summary:
NASA's Voyager 1 has just become the first human-made object ever to travel one light-day from Earth — roughly 16.1 billion miles away. A radio signal takes a full 24 hours to travel from Earth to the spacecraft and back.

But the nearly 50-year-old probe hit a snag just as it reached the milestone. On November 14, the team discovered that the spacecraft had stopped sending science data back to Earth. As of November 19, the problem had not been solved.

There is good news, though. The team detected a 'carrier' signal, which confirmed that Voyager 1 is powered up and pointed in the right direction. Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd said she is 'confident' the science data will start flowing again soon.

NASA thinks the glitch comes from the probe's onboard computer. The team faced a similar problem in November 2023 and fixed it in June 2024. They are tackling this glitch the same way.

If the fix works, Voyager 1 will keep sending data from its two remaining science instruments, a magnetometer and a plasma wave detector.
why_it_matters: Voyager 1 is the only spacecraft sending back news from between the stars, so fixing it helps us learn about space.
